chunks: Ali, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man who is in a state of major ritual impurity immerses himself in water with a single immersion, and then comes out; would that suffice him for his ritual bath?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: To be in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)

ai.seo_question: Is one immersion sufficient for ghusl if one is in a state of major ritual impurity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the minimal requirement for ghusl al-janabah, affirming that a single complete immersion (irtimas) suffices for ritual purity, a ruling derived from the principle of ease in purification rituals. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus that the essence of ghusl is the washing of the entire body with water, rather than the number of repetitions, thereby distinguishing it from more rigorous practices found in other schools. This narration is frequently cited in discussions on the sufficiency of water volume and the mechanics of ritual bathing in fiqh manuals.
